executiveSummary: GM0417's identity, Gooi en Vechtstreek safety-region assignment, full 2025 boundary and CBS resident control are coherent. Fresh context reports 11,474 residents; ten published neighbourhood rows sum to 11,470 (-4, -0.035%), a negligible difference that preserves CBS rounding and suppression semantics. The bundle contains one district, ten neighbourhoods, one BAG place and one BRT woonkern. Seven logical motorway records represent portions of only two physical corridors, A1 and A27; these series/junction edges are non-additive. No ProRail station lies inside the municipality and 16 scheduled-transit stop areas are present. All ten presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services and pass structural/numerical contracts. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Official Laren and AGV evidence distinguishes high-area infiltration, low-area street/sewer surcharge and groundwater, the Gooiergracht drainage route toward Eemmeer, and wastewater transfer to RWZI Blaricum. The generic Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset instead holds 0.446750 normalized inundation stress through T+72, increasing affected residents from 512 to 691 without a named connected water source, boundary/control state, footprint, arrival or recession. Coastal water is zero but only for the configured narrow source, not an all-clear. Eight unrelated non-earthquake presets reuse exactly the same complete neighbourhood order, always led by five-resident Laren-Natuurgebied, including river, heat and cyber. A controlled fire source inside that neighbourhood can create direct flame, but canonical wildfire has zero local flame and unverified transported smoke despite current authoritative heath/woodland and dated drought/fire-risk evidence. Exact mobility, utilities, acute care, wastewater, supply and recovery remain unsupported by live topology, state, capacity, backup, resources and actions. Missing observations, forecasts and local registry matches are Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.title: E01 — Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025, table 86165NED, OData API
supports: The official municipality row identifies GM0417 Laren (NH.) and reports 11,474 residents, density 925 per square kilometre, 32.5% age 65 or older and 1,955 one-person households.

The ten published neighbourhood rows sum to 11,470 residents (-4, -0.035%), 5,165 households and 3,745 residents aged 65 or older; the negligible difference retains annual rounding and suppression semantics.

Most fields cover all ten neighbourhoods. Home value, tenure, cars per household, benefits/pensions, doctor/supermarket distance and population density cover nine, while district-heating share and public-charging counts cover zero and must not become zero.

CBS OData is machine-readable under CC BY 4.0, with quarterly additions described for this annual table. It controls residents, not incident-time visitors, pupils, patients, commuters, responders, individual vulnerability or preparedness.

evidenceSources.publisher: PDOK / CBS / Kadaster / Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi
evidenceSources.title: E02 — Full municipal geometry, settlement and road, rail and scheduled-transit reference inputs
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 boundary/statistics and current generated BAG, BRT, NWB, ProRail and GTFS snapshots
supports: The generated centre [5.216473054119728, 52.24228531527495] lies inside the fresh full-resolution 2025 municipal boundary.
The bundle retains one district, ten neighbourhoods, one BAG place named Laren and one BRT woonkern; no BAG place centre falls outside the generalized boundary.

Seven logical road records are portions of only A1 and A27. Four A1 and three A27 records share their respective physical-corridor identities and are boundary/junction series, not seven independent evacuation or supply paths.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Wateroverlast and Laren Regenklaar implementation context
evidenceSources.edition: Current public guidance and programme pages inspected 3 September 2026; Omgevingsvisie Laren 2040 adopted 17 December 2025
supports: Laren says intense rain can exceed sewer capacity. In Hoog Laren the programme redirects roof and street water toward local infiltration, including vertical infiltration; in parts of Laag Laren heavy rain leaves water on streets and can force mainly rainwater from the sewer into gardens/public space through relief points.

Months of rain can saturate the ground and raise groundwater into older basements/crawl spaces; the municipality continuously measures selected wells but states groundwater is complex, interventions are conditional and responsibilities are shared.

Laren Regenklaar includes public- and private-space measures whose installation and maintenance state varies. A project or maintenance instruction is not proof of event-time storage, infiltration, inlet/sewer capacity or correct operation.

The current environmental vision calls for rain/heat-ready neighbourhoods and protection of the green outer area. Planning ambition is not a hazard raster, live observation, probability or T+72 response.
The inspected web/PDF routes do not expose a stable machine API with guaranteed refresh, blanket reuse licence, native raster metadata and explicit NoData contract.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Amstel, Gooi en Vecht / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Gooiergracht drainage, wastewater dependency and public water-asset context
evidenceSources.edition: Project page last updated February 2026; draft plan announced 23 April 2026; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: The Gooiergracht borders Laren/Blaricum/Eemnes and carries water from the Gooi toward Eemmeer through five weirs and gemaal Gooiergracht. It is a managed drainage/receiving-water pathway, not the Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset's generic local depth.

AGV says the system has longstanding heavy-rain water nuisance, drought/water-shortage, vulnerable banks and maintenance issues. Its 2026 draft plan proposes fixed target levels, controllable replacement weirs, watercourse/culvert widening and nature-friendly banks; draft measures are not completed protection or current operating state.
AGV states wastewater from Laren, Blaricum and Eemnes is treated at RWZI Blaricum. This creates a real cross-boundary sewer/energy/access dependency absent from a municipal scalar.

The partial HWH/PDOK registry assigns only one realized weir to GM0417, with null capacity. It is a contributor-dependent national aggregation under CC BY-SA 4.0 and plainly does not represent the complete Gooiergracht, sewer, pump or treatment chain.
No public page establishes connected catchments, comparable capacity, current level/flow, weir/pump command, blockage, power/backup or T+72 restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel Gooi en Vechtstreek 2024 and first-72-hour preparedness
evidenceSources.edition: Definitive 2024 risk profile, policy basis for 2025–2028; national preparedness guidance current at access
supports: The four-year regional profile prioritizes storm/wind/rain, cold, heat, flooding, nature fire, electricity loss, speech/data loss, cyberattack and transport incidents. Regional eligibility is not a Laren event probability, footprint or magnitude.

It identifies forests/heath and recreation, hospitals and less-self-reliant facilities, visitor venues, intensive road/rail movement and cross-boundary vital-service effects. It also highlights ageing, one-person households and people living independently whose needs are not known address by address.

Nature fire became a priority because climate change raises probability and impact; cyber and ICT coupling can propagate service failures. These are planning mechanisms, not a current ignition, target compromise, outage or restoration curve.

The strategic PDF has no standard machine incident/resource endpoint or stated blanket reuse licence/cadence. It validates preparedness scope, never staffing, stock, dispatch, backup or action completion.

National guidance advises a 72-hour emergency kit including three litres of water per person per day, food, medicine, radio/power and a personal plan. Guidance does not prove household readiness or local distribution capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Goois Natuurreservaat / Waterschap Amstel, Gooi en Vecht
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Laren heath, woodland and visitor context with dated 2026 drought/fire-risk state
evidenceSources.edition: Current area pages; GNR drought report 11 August 2026; AGV restriction update 25 August 2026
supports: GNR identifies Westerheide in Hilversum/Laren as 344 hectares of heath and woodland with day recreation, and De Postiljon in Laren as 37 hectares of woodland, inland dunes and heath. This establishes fuel/interface and visitor eligibility, not an ignition or people count.

GNR reported on 11 August 2026 that prolonged drought affected higher Gooise-ridge soils and nature-fire danger was very high. AGV lifted surface-water and groundwater abstraction bans effective 26/28 August after rain but said the water deficit remained concerning.

Those dated states must expire at their valid times: they do not prove the current official fire phase on 3 September, fuel moisture, a local ignition/perimeter, smoke plume, access, extinguishing-water availability or suppression resources.

A controlled T+24 model source at [5.213170057836248, 52.231038038451274] inside Laren-Natuurgebied produces direct fire 0.686123 and smoke 0.533028 and ranks the containing neighbourhood first. This is a synthetic containment test, not validation by the public evidence.
GNR/AGV pages do not state a stable machine incident API, fixed refresh or blanket data reuse licence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Provincie Noord-Holland / Rijkswaterstaat / Tergooi MC / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Gooi bus concession, A1/A27 access and cross-boundary acute care
evidenceSources.edition: Gooi en Vechtstreek concession current through end-2030; NWB-Light 1 August 2026; RIVM questionnaire 2026 v1.1
supports: Noord-Holland is the competent authority for the Gooi en Vechtstreek bus concession, currently operated by Connexxion/Transdev through end-2030. A concession and GTFS stops do not prove a trip operates or can carry emergency demand at the exercise time.

The generated graph exposes A1/A27 boundary series but not a complete local N525/urban/nature access network, bus operation, pedestrian/cycle access or incident restrictions. Scenario-unit ceilings 260 are neither measured vehicles/hour nor additive across repeated corridor sections.

Rijkswaterstaat's A1 Eemnes–Muiderberg closure ended 17 August 2026 and therefore must not affect a 3 September reference run; the published summer-2027 opposite-direction phase likewise cannot be promoted to current restriction. This demonstrates the need for issue/start/end time.

RIVM assigns no emergency department inside GM0417. Tergooi MC Hilversum is about 6.16 kilometres straight-line from the representative centre; RIVM v1.1 reports 24/7 ED/acute obstetrics, seventeen treatment rooms and 26,161 visits in 2025, and Tergooi confirms a new access road opened 19 June 2026.

Annual facility facts and completed access works do not establish incident route time, ambulance availability, acceptance/diversion, staffing, occupancy, generator endurance or live capacity. RIVM data are CC0 1.0; project/operation pages do not supply a machine incident contract.

evidenceSources.publisher: Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / KNMI / Rijkswaterstaat / RIVM / NDW
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public grid-planning, antenna, education, warning, water, care and observation screens
supports: One postcode sample, 1251GB, maps to Liander area OS CRAILO 10-1i: withdrawal existing/required/queue 36/20/0.6 MW with seven queued requests, injection 36/9/7 MW with request count null, and 28 projects from 2026. Null remains Unknown, never zero.

The sample is large-user planning/queue context, not complete municipality/feeder coverage, live load, reserve, outage, switching or restoration. Capacity/projects update at least quarterly and queues monthly; its frontend endpoint is not a stable API contract and an exact dataset licence identifier was not found.

The screens contain 21 RDI antenna sites—sixteen mobile, two fixed-link, two amateur and one broadcast—and eleven DUO education records—four primary, four secondary and three other. Registers do not establish coverage/backhaul/power, occupants, shelter role, accessibility, supplies or operation.

No GM0417 government-service, seismic, NDW situation, RIVM acute-care/PM2.5, KNMI weather-station or Waterinfo observation/forecast point is assigned. The province-level warning record is explicit no-warning at issue time, not gridded local forcing or an all-clear for an arbitrary exercise.

RDI cadence/licence is unstated; DUO snapshot 31 August is daily under CC Attribution version unspecified; KNMI is CC BY 4.0; Waterinfo/NDW and RIVM acute care are CC0. All public-context sources remain affectsSimulation=false.

notes: River severity/stress and seven services remain fixed from T+24 to T+72, affected rises 512 to 691 and Facilities falls 0.817359 to 0.738428, accumulating 137,502.852 person-hours without a water boundary, recession, access or action.

Sustained disruption and recovery can be plausible, but exact first-72-hour values require selected incidents, measured/modelled state, constraints, resources and actions.

Plans, dated notices, observations, forecasts, registers, nulls/missing matches and model outputs display evidence class, validity, licence, affectsSimulation, uncertainty and Unknown/NoData.

residualLimitations: Complete electricity, gas, drinking-water, sewer/drainage, telecom, care and supply topology, control logic, live load/outage, backup, crews, spares, fuel and restoration state are unavailable or security-sensitive; public geometry, plans and territories cannot replace them.

No selected AGV/WMCN/LIWO case establishes a GM0417 Rhine/Meuse/IJssel or Eem/Eemmeer/Gooiergracht boundary, defence/control state, terrain-connected footprint, depth/velocity, arrival or recession. A generic value is not evidence and no selected case is not safe.

Laren Regenklaar and Gooiergracht products are valuable official programme/scenario evidence but require native machine files, edition, event/antecedent state, CRS, units, licence, lifecycle and explicit NoData before analytical use.

The HWH screen contains one null-capacity weir despite AGV's broader five-weir/gemaal description. Neither source supplies complete sewer/catchment/RWZI connectivity, settings, maintenance, power/backup, current state or event capacity.
No local Waterinfo observation/forecast point is assigned. Missing point/horizon coverage cannot be spatialized, held constant or treated as zero through T+72.

A1/A27 NWB edges, local road omissions, 16 GTFS stops and zero NDW situations do not establish scenario-time operation, passability, emergency priority, detours, destination or throughput. Repeated motorway sections are not independent redundancy.

RIVM/Tergooi records do not expose incident-time ambulance availability, staffing, dispatch, acceptance/diversion, occupancy, backup or restoration; protected operational information must not be inferred.

CBS residents omit patients, care residents, pupils, commuters, workers, GNR/Singer/sports visitors, volunteers and responders. Rounded/suppressed aggregates cannot identify individuals, preparedness or event presence.

The 11 August very-high nature-fire notice and 25 August drought update are dated state, not a current fire phase, ignition, perimeter, spread or smoke forecast. They must expire rather than be projected through an arbitrary scenario.
One Liander planning sample is neither municipal coverage nor outage evidence. Its null request count is Unknown, not zero; sensitive topology must not be reconstructed publicly.
Antenna and education registers have different spatial support, cadence and licences and remain affectsSimulation=false without verified causal bindings.
No-warning and no locally assigned water/weather/road/care/PM2.5/seismic/government point are coverage/time facts, not zero hazard, disruption, pollution, need or service continuity.

Exact hazard, affected-population, service, recovery and person-hour outputs remain synthetic exercises, not observations, forecasts, operator commitments or decision-grade advice until critical/high findings are corrected and authorities review the case.
This audit covers only the first 72 hours. Groundwater, wildfire ecosystem effects, wastewater interruption, care disruption and infrastructure recovery can persist much longer.
provinceReviewFlags: Noord-Holland, VRGV, AGV and GM0417 should define expert selection/versioning for external major water, Eemmeer/Gooiergracht backwater and local pluvial/groundwater cases, including high/low terrain, receiving/control state, units, footprint, arrival/recession, uncertainty and NoData.

AGV and BEL sewer/water teams should review privacy-safe Gooiergracht, infiltration, sewer-relief, gemaal/weir and RWZI Blaricum dependency contracts, including power/control/manual fallback and first-72-hour actions without exposing sensitive topology.

Province, Rijkswaterstaat, municipality, Transdev and emergency partners should review A1/A27/N525/local approaches, buses and nature access as direction- and mode-specific, non-additive, valid-time care/supply/evacuation/fire/repair routes.

Municipality, GNR, fire service, GHOR, ambulance provider and Tergooi should review current fire-phase/source/plume, visitor presence, access/firewater/suppression and privacy-safe care continuity through protected interfaces rather than dated public inference.

Gooi en Vechtstreek partners should turn 72-hour preparedness into typed but activation-gated warning, household/welfare support, evacuation/shelter, medical, utility, wastewater, supply, fire and recovery actions, separating plan, project, observation, forecast, official scenario, live state, synthetic assumption and Unknown.
